title: Spotticus
description:
Leftover included coding-agent quota is spare capacity. Interactive work is on-demand. Interruptible Kanbus chores (spot tasks) fill leftover before reset and preempt when a human needs the pool.

Two jobs: (1) curated leftover probes for products Anthus uses, (2) dispatch policy including per-product clocks and the assumption that one agentic run may burn a whole remaining window.

Not Fast. Not on-demand spend. Not always-be-agenting. Not a second queue beside Kanbus.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Iteration 1 scope: one working Claude leftover probe via CodexBar + spare-pace scoring. No dispatch, no multi-product, no daemon.

Architecture decisions settled:
1. Window model: dict[str, WindowUsage] keyed by canonical name (not primary/secondary). Antigravity has 4+ windows that don't fit a flat model.
2. CodexBar coupling: call codexbar usage --format json (all providers), parse per-provider in a pure function. One subprocess call, one parse seam.
3. Sync for iteration 1. CLI is the only caller. Async is iteration 2.
4. Scoring: takes WindowUsage (carries resets_at for elapsed calc). Thresholds as function args with defaults. Per-product config is iteration 2.
5. CLI: probe + spare as separate subcommands. Different concerns, different exit codes.
6. Tests: manual Gherkin-to-pytest mapping. No pytest-bdd dependency. Keep deps minimal.

Stashed prototype is available as reference (git stash: iter1-prototype-code-before-planning).

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Pivot Iteration 1 Architecture (based on user feedback):
1. Window model: Single ordered list of windows (list[WindowUsage]) with metadata (name, is_session, is_weekly).
2. Scope: Parse all providers returned by CodexBar, not just one.
3. CLI: High-level UI that looks across all accounts to find dispatch opportunities (e.g., `spotticus opportunities` or `spotticus status`).
4. Scoring nuance: A provider is ONLY eligible if ALL of its windows are spare.
5. Implementation: Write fresh code, use stashed prototype only for JSON fixtures.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Iteration 1 completed. Code merged to develop. CLI `status` command is fully functional for dispatch evaluations across all accounts.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Iteration 2 scope: Lock Management and Preemption.
Spotticus acts as a Dispatch Oracle and Lock Manager.
1. `claim`: requires agent metadata (--pid, --product, --model, --name, optional --session-id). Writes lockfile.
2. `release`: clears lockfile on clean exit.
3. `hold`: sends SIGTERM to the locked PID, sets a persistent HOLD lock.
4. `status`: updated to evaluate lock state (locked/held pools are ineligible).

comments.author: home
comments.text: Iteration 2 complete. Lock Management and Preemption shipped. Agents can now safely claim, release, and hold pools using Spotticus as a Dispatch Oracle.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Iteration 3 scope: Multi-Tank Pools.
1. Parse `extraRateWindows` in CodexBar output.
2. Group windows into logical `Pool` objects (e.g., antigravity:gemini, cursor:premium).
3. Locks and claims apply to `provider:pool` instead of just `provider`.
4. Scoring evaluates eligibility per-pool, meaning a depleted Claude tank no longer blocks the Gemini tank.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Iteration 3 complete. Multi-Tank Pools shipped. Agents can now claim specific model tanks independently.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Iteration 4 scope: Target Filtering & Optimization.
1. Add `--target` flag to `spotticus status` (can be specified multiple times).
2. Probe layer extracts unique base providers and fetches ONLY those via `codexbar usage --provider X`.
3. Output layer prunes pools that were not explicitly requested, saving context window tokens.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Iteration 4 complete. Target Filtering shipped. Spotticus now correctly filters and prunes output based on the --target flag.
